ORCHESTRATOR DECISION (mandate 6329234399, scope all, session s4): this withdraws route 1. Do these steps.
(1) Remove the alias. Keep the corrected comment and the narrative fix, which the reviewer found sound.
(2) Look for a REAL payment of seam_cut_total. That means removing a genuine cross-seam dependency (move, share or refactor code) that tools/audit/archscore/ score.py, run before and after, does not read as worse, and that judgement finds sounder. An alias or a re-binding is not a payment. Record each payment you try, with its dS.

Do it under 0013 and the mandate above, with the body section `## Raise justification`. That section lists each payment tried and an `Architecture score: dS <value>` line. Do not use --record and raise no other leaf.
(4) The pr-contract red: carry_audit.py refused the `## Friction` item, because `Carry: orchestrator.md section 5` is not a destination. Route it as `<GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>`. Run `python3 tools/audit/carry_audit.py check --body <body>` locally until it reports 0 unrouted and 0 bad.
(5) `## Red checks` names pr-contract (jobs 120045400798 and 120032771136). Its cheaper detector is carry_audit check --body run before the push, so state that and answer it.
(6) Route the reviewer's instrument finding under `## Findings` or `## Forward-carry`. The finding: structure.py counts cross-seam attribute OCCURRENCES, not distinct attributes (~L1076-1118), so any local alias games seam_cut_total. Route it to the roster group that owns tests/structure.py. Search dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json on origin/main and origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster. If no such group exists, carry it as a new O<n> on R10-CURRENCY and say so explicitly. Do NOT fix structure.py here.
